chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to us, he said: One of our companions narrated to me, from Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, when the servants sleep, their spirits exit toward the heaven. So what the spirit sees in the heaven is the truth, and what it sees in the atmosphere are confused dreams.

Verily, the spirits are enlisted soldiers. So whichever of them recognizes the other unites with it, and whichever of them finds the other unfamiliar diverges from it. So when the spirit is in the heaven, they recognize each other and they loathe each other. And when they recognize each other in the heaven, they recognize each other on earth; and when they loathe each other in the heaven, they loathe each other on earth.

key_terms.الأرواح: Arwah (spirits/souls) — the non-physical essence of humans that departs during sleep
key_terms.الأضغاث: Adghath (confused dreams) — meaningless or jumbled dream imagery, contrasted with true visions from the heaven
key_terms.جنود مجندة: Junud mujannada (enlisted soldiers) — a famous expression indicating that souls were grouped and organized in a pre-worldly existence

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about the nature of souls during sleep and why people feel natural affinity or aversion toward others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) explains the metaphysical nature of human souls during sleep. He teaches that spirits ascend to the heavens when a person sleeps, and true visions come from what the spirit perceives in the heavens, while confused dreams come from the lower atmosphere. He then introduces the famous prophetic concept that souls are like enlisted soldiers grouped together — those that share an innate familiarity unite, while those that are strangers to each other diverge. This teaching was originally delivered to Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, a close companion, and explains the spiritual basis for natural human affinities and antipathies.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ya`qub b. Yazid narrated to us. He said: One of our companions narrated to me from Zakariyya b. Yahya from Mu`awiyah b. `Ammar from Abu Ja`far.  He said:
When the servants sleep, their spirits exit towards the heaven. So, what the spirit sees in the heaven, is true. And what it sees in the atmosphere, it is far from reality.

Now surely the spirits are enlisted soldiers [of an army]. Then whichever of them gets acquainted with the other, it unites [with the other] and whichever of them rejects the other, it diverges [from the other]. So, when the spirit is in the heaven, it gets acquainted [with another] and it loathes [another, mutually]. And when they are acquainted in the heaven, they are acquainted on Earth and when they loathe each other in the heaven, they loathe each other on earth.
